findings.title: L1->L2 migration redemption has no spent-marker and uses += accounting, allowing unbounded replay of a single proof/signature to mint unbacked deposits, stalk and roots
findings.description: redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances() is the permissionless L2 endpoint that re-issues an L1 contract's silo deposits, stalk and roots onto L2. It verifies a Merkle proof against a static MERKLE_ROOT and an EIP-712 signature (signed on L1) but never records that a given (owner, leaf, signature) has been redeemed. After verification it writes per-account deposits, then calls setStalk(reciever, accountStalk, ownerRoots) which does `s.accts[reciever].stalk += accountStalk` and `s.accts[reciever].roots += accountRoots`. Because there is no nonce/spent mapping and stalk/roots accumulate with +=, the exact same calldata (owner, reciever, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots, proof, deadline, signature) can be resubmitted any number of times until `deadline`. Each replay re-adds accountStalk and ownerRoots, and re-writes the deposit entries. The proof and signature are fully public (visible in the original L2 transaction calldata / mempool), so no privileged material is required to replay. This is a cross-chain bug because the authorization artifact (the L1-signed permit + L1 Merkle leaf) is intended to be consumed exactly once on L2 but the L2 contract enforces no consume-once semantics.
findings.impact: An attacker observes any legitimate migration redemption (or front-runs one), then replays the identical calldata repeatedly. stalk and roots are inflated without backing on each replay; stalk and roots are the governance vote weight and the divisor/numerator for earned-Bean (mint) distribution. Unbounded inflation of stalk/roots dilutes all honest holders' yield and grants the replayer effectively unlimited governance weight and an outsized claim on every future sunrise mint — protocol insolvency / unbacked share issuance. Critical under Immunefi v2.2 (direct theft of protocol value / unbacked minting of value-bearing shares).
findings.proof_of_concept:
Foundry steps (fork L2 after migration facet wired):
1. L1 owner signs the EIP-712 permit and a valid Merkle leaf exists; a first call to redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances(owner, reciever, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots, proof, deadline, sig) succeeds. Record s.accts[reciever].stalk (S0) and .roots (R0) via vm.load on the account slots.
2. From a different EOA, resubmit the identical calldata. Assert it does NOT revert (no spent marker).
3. After N replays assert s.accts[reciever].stalk == S0 + N*delta and .roots == R0 + N*deltaRoots (vm.load before/after).
4. Call the earned-Bean distribution / governance weight getter for `reciever` and assert the inflated value is consumed (outcome layer).
All three layers (EOA entry, storage flip on stalk/roots, economic outcome of inflated share) are assertable.

findings.title: BeanL1RecieverFacet caps migrated L1 Beans at EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS = 0, so every L2 mint reverts after the user's L1 Beans are already burned (permanent cross-chain fund loss)
findings.description: The L1->L2 Bean migration is a burn-then-mint cross-chain flow: BeanL2MigrationFacet.migrateL2Beans() calls C.bean().burnFrom(msg.sender, amount) on L1 and then relays a cross-chain message to BeanL1RecieverFacet.recieveL1Beans(reciever, amount) on L2. On L2, recieveL1Beans does `s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans += amount;` then `require(EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS >= s.sys.migration.migratedL1Beans, ...)` before `C.bean().mint(reciever, amount)`. EXTERNAL_L1_BEANS is a hardcoded constant equal to 0. For any amount > 0 the post-increment value of migratedL1Beans is positive, so the require evaluates `0 >= positive` = false and reverts. The L1 burn has already executed and is not rolled back on L2 (separate chains, asynchronous message). Therefore every honest external Bean migrant loses their L1 Beans with no corresponding L2 issuance.
findings.impact: Direct, permanent loss of all externally-held L1 Beans that attempt migration: L1 burn succeeds, the corresponding L2 mint always reverts because the migration cap is 0. No attacker is required; the migration path is fully bricked and every user who uses it loses funds. Critical under Immunefi v2.2 (permanent loss of user funds).

Foundry steps:
1. On the L1 side, give an EOA Bean balance and approval; call migrateL2Beans(reciever, L2Beanstalk, amount=1e6, gasLimit). Assert C.bean().balanceOf(user) decreased by amount (burn occurred).
2. On the L2 side, impersonate BRIDGE (0x4200...0007) and mock xDomainMessageSender() == L1BEANSTALK, then call recieveL1Beans(reciever, 1e6).
3. Assert the call reverts with 'L2Migration: exceeds maximum migrated' (require 0 >= 1e6 is false).
4. Outcome: L1 Beans burned, L2 mint reverted -> net supply destroyed for the user. Assert reciever's L2 Bean balance == 0.

findings.title: L2ContractMigrationFacet zeroes global per-token silo balances on every redeem
findings.description: addMigratedDepositsToAccount declares local uint128 totalDeposited and totalDepositedBdv (lines 159-160) but never increments them inside the deposit loop. After crediting per-account deposits, lines 194-195 assign these still-zero locals to the protocol-wide totals s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited and .depositedBdv. The redeem entry point (redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances) is permissionless (anyone with a valid proof+signature can call it), so the global silo balance for every migrated token is overwritten to 0 on each call, while per-account deposit records (s.accts[account].deposits[depositId]) are written correctly and remain non-zero. This is a hard assignment (=), not an increment, so it also clobbers whatever ReseedSilo previously set. Independently verified against source: locals are declared and never written before being stored to global state.
findings.impact: Global deposited/depositedBdv for every token routed through contract migration is set to 0 while per-account deposits exist, breaking the core invariant total == sum(accounts) (ACC-002). Downstream consumers that read s.sys.silo.balances[token] for BDV ratios, convert valuation, gauge weighting and withdrawal accounting are corrupted protocol-wide: a depositor whose token total reads 0 cannot have their withdrawal decrement reconciled (DoS / underflow), and BDV/convert math that scales by global deposited can be skewed to mint unbacked BDV/stalk. Permissionless, deterministic, protocol-wide accounting corruption with no rescue path short of a governance upgrade.
findings.proof_of_concept: 1) Attacker (or any migrant) crafts a valid proof+signature for an owner with deposits in token T. 2) Calls redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances. 3) vm.load(silo.balances[T].deposited) before/after: non-zero -> 0. 4) Outcome: a subsequent SiloFacet.withdrawDeposit for any holder of T attempts to decrement the (now 0) global total -> underflow revert (token withdrawals bricked) OR convert/BDV reads scaled by 0 misprice. Assert global total == 0 while sum of per-account deposit.amount > 0.
findings.recommendation: Accumulate totalDeposited += depositData.amounts[i] and totalDepositedBdv += depositData.bdvs[i] inside the loop, and use += (not =) when writing to s.sys.silo.balances[token] so concurrent reseed/migration paths do not clobber each other. Add an invariant check that the post-write global total equals the sum of all migrated deposits.

findings.recommendation: Persist a spent-marker keyed by the merkle leaf (or the blueprint of owner+reciever+deadline) and/or a per-owner nonce inside the EIP-712 struct hash; check-and-set it before crediting. Reject any redemption whose marker is already set so each authorization is consumable exactly once.
findings.description: L2ContractMigrationFacet.redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances is an external, permissionless function (only nonReentrant). It authenticates a migration by (1) MerkleProof.verify over leaf=keccak256(account,deposits,internalBalances,ownerRoots) against a hardcoded MERKLE_ROOT, and (2) an EIP-712 signature over (owner,reciever,deadline) recovered with ECDSA.recover and required to equal owner. Neither check consumes any state: there is no nonce, no per-leaf/per-signature redeemed-marker, and no per-account migration flag. All inputs (proof and signature) are plain calldata, visible on-chain the moment the first legitimate redemption is broadcast. setStalk uses `s.accts[account].stalk += accountStalk` and `s.accts[account].roots += accountRoots` (line 205-211), and addMigratedDepositsToAccount re-writes the same deposit slots each call. Because both the proof and the signature re-validate identically on every call, anyone can resubmit the exact observed calldata repeatedly until `deadline`, accumulating stalk and roots to `reciever` on each replay while no L1 backing is consumed (the L1 deposits are not burned per-redemption by this function). The result is unbounded inflation of governance/yield weight (stalk drives Stalk-weighted governance and Silo earnings; roots drive earned-bean distribution) and per-account deposit credit, against the protocol invariant that migrated credit is issued exactly once per L1 owner. This is the access-control failure mode of signature reuse: a one-time authorization is treated as a reusable capability.
findings.impact: Repeated replay of a single legitimate migration's public calldata inflates s.accts[reciever].stalk and s.accts[reciever].roots without bound (and re-credits deposits), corrupting Stalk-weighted governance, Silo earnings, and earned-bean accounting protocol-wide. Conservative reading: unbacked minting of governance weight and yield -> protocol insolvency / governance capture. Immunefi v2.2: protocol insolvency / unbacked value creation = High to Critical; scored High pending PoC of the economic magnitude.

From any EOA, resubmit the identical calldata before `deadline`. verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances passes (same leaf, same root). verifySignature passes (same digest, signer==owner). 3. setStalk runs again: reciever.stalk and reciever.roots increase by the same delta a second time. 4. Repeat N times within the deadline window. Assert s.accts[reciever].stalk after N calls == N * delta (vm.load on the stalk slot) while no L1 burn/lock counter increased. findings.title: LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice NatSpec states lookback>0 returns TWAP, but the ternary returns spot for lookback>0 and divides-by-zero for lookback==0
findings.description: The NatSpec on getTokenPrice (lines 34-36) explicitly documents the intended behavior: 'Use lookback = 0 for the instantaneous price. lookback > 0 for a TWAP.' and 'Returns 0 if priceAggregatorAddress is broken or frozen.' The code implements the exact opposite mapping: `return lookback > 0 ? getPrice(...) : getTwap(..., lookback)`. getPrice is the instantaneous/spot path and getTwap is the lookback-windowed path, so a caller requesting a manipulation-resistant TWAP (lookback>0) silently receives a flash-loan-manipulable spot price, and a caller requesting spot (lookback==0) invokes getTwap with lookback=0 whose final statement is `t.cumulativePrice.mul(PRECISION).div(10 ** decimals).div(lookback)` — a division by zero that REVERTS rather than returning the documented 0 sentinel. Both halves of the NatSpec contract are violated: the value semantics are inverted, and the documented frozen-feed graceful-degradation guarantee does not hold on the lookback==0 path.
findings.impact: Any internal consumer that follows the documented convention and passes lookback>0 expecting manipulation resistance instead consumes the instantaneous spot price. If a reachable mint/convert/peg path (LibEthUsdOracle -> LibWellMinting/LibDeltaB -> sunrise Bean issuance / convert valuation) requests a TWAP through this function, single-block flash-loan reserve/price skew mispriced Bean issuance and conversions. The lookback==0 spot path additionally bricks (reverts) instead of degrading, contradicting the '@dev Returns 0 if broken or frozen' guarantee for that path.

ite.technique: Ternary branches transposed; consumer relying on lookback>0 for safety receives manipulable spot. Spot request (lookback==0) reverts via div-by-zero.
ite.evasion: The inversion defeats the only manipulation guard; a flash-loan attacker requests/relies on a path the protocol believes is TWAP-protected.

findings.title: Migration Merkle leaf omits reciever, so any holder of the public L1 signature can redirect another contract's migration credit to an attacker-chosen L2 address
findings.description: verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances() computes the Merkle leaf as keccak256(abi.encode(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots)) — it commits to the L1 owner and the asset data but NOT to reciever. reciever (the L2 destination of the credit) is bound only by the separate EIP-712 signature in verifySignature() over (owner, reciever, deadline). The signature is presented in the public L2 transaction calldata. Combined with CC-001's lack of replay protection, the (owner, reciever, deadline) tuple and signature are observable on-chain, and because the Merkle proof does not constrain reciever, the redeem function will accept any reciever for which a matching signature is presented. There is no on-chain link forcing reciever to equal the original migrant, so credit can be steered to an attacker address as part of a replay.
findings.impact: The migration deposit/stalk/roots credit for an L1 contract can be redirected to and/or duplicated at an attacker-chosen L2 address using the publicly visible signature, rather than only the originally intended reciever. Standalone this is an authorization-binding gap; combined with CC-001 it converts replay into attacker-controlled theft of migrated value. High (Critical when chained with CC-001).

findings.title: Flood (Season of Plenty) mints and dumps Beans sized by instantaneous well reserves and swaps with zero slippage, enabling flash-loan over-mint + sandwich of stalkholder proceeds
findings.description: During a Flood, SeasonFacet.gm() -> calcCaseIdandUpdate() -> LibFlood.handleRain() takes the else (flood) branch and calls getWellsByDeltaB(), which derives each well's deltaB from LibDeltaB.currentDeltaB(well) -> IWell(well).getReserves(). These are the INSTANTANEOUS spot reserves of the Well, not the manipulation-resistant cumulative-pump TWAP that the sunrise mint uses (LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB / readTwaReserves). calculateSopPerWell() converts that instantaneous positive deltaB directly into the Bean amount to mint, then sopWell() does C.bean().mint(this, sopBeans) followed by IWell(well).swapFrom(bean, sopToken, sopBeans, 0, this, type(uint256).max) — minAmountOut hardcoded to 0 and deadline to max. The non-Bean proceeds (e.g. WETH) are distributed to Stalkholders via rewardSop(). Because the entire SOP size and the swap price both come from the live, single-block-manipulable Well state, a flood season is a deterministic, permissionlessly-triggerable MEV event: (1) an attacker who pushes the Well's Bean reserve down (raising instantaneous deltaB) immediately before the sunrise tx inflates sopBeans, and (2) the zero-minAmountOut swap can be sandwiched so the attacker buys the dumped Beans cheaply / sells the scarce non-Bean token, extracting value that should have become stalkholder plenty. The flood is triggerable by anyone via the permissionless sunrise/gm() once Beanstalk has been Oversaturated for a season, so the attacker controls the timing.
findings.impact: Stalkholders receive materially less SOP plenty than the Flood mints; the shortfall is captured by the MEV/sandwich actor. Combined with instantaneous-reserve sizing, an attacker can also force a larger Bean mint+dump than the protocol intends, deepening the post-flood depeg. Value-at-risk per flood scales with Well liquidity and the depth of the reserve skew; on a deep Bean:ETH well a single flood can leak a large fraction of the SOP proceeds. No privileged access required.
findings.proof_of_concept:
Preconditions: Beanstalk is Oversaturated (P>1, pod rate <5%) and was raining last season, so the next sunrise will Flood. Soppable well = Bean:WETH, instantaneous deltaB ~ +200,000 Bean at honest reserves.
1. Attacker observes the pending sunrise()/gm() (or front-runs the season boundary).
2. In the same block, BEFORE the sunrise tx: flash-loan WETH and buy Beans from the Bean:WETH well, lowering the Bean reserve. This raises currentDeltaB(well) read by getWellsByDeltaB() to, e.g., +260,000 (over-mint of ~60,000 Bean).
3. sunrise()/gm() executes: LibFlood.sopWell() mints 260,000 Bean and calls swapFrom(bean->WETH, 260000e6, minAmountOut=0). With the reserve already skewed and no slippage floor, the protocol sells its freshly minted Beans into the attacker-degraded curve at a poor rate.
4. Attacker back-runs: sell the Beans bought in step 2 back / unwind the flash loan, pocketing the spread plus the WETH the protocol under-received. The WETH credited to Stalkholders via rewardSop() (amount.mul(SOP_PRECISION).div(rain.roots)) is reduced by the same spread.
Net: attacker profit = (WETH extracted from the zero-slippage protocol swap) - (flash-loan fee + gas); positive whenever the skew exceeds swap fees, which deep wells easily permit. Stalkholder plenty falls by the same amount.

findings.description: ReseedSilo.init() re-seeds the L2 silo by calling reseedSiloDeposit() once per whitelisted token (BEAN, BEAN:ETH, BEAN:wstETH, BEAN:3CRV, urBEAN, urBEAN:LP). findings.title: L1->L2 reseed never initializes global Silo total stalk/roots (s.sys.silo.stalk / s.sys.silo.roots), breaking the protocol-wide stalk-conservation invariant and corrupting roots/earned-Bean accounting for the entire migrated population

During the L1->L2 reseed, ReseedSilo.reseedSiloDeposit issues per-account stalk (s.accts[account].stalk = accountStalk) and per-token global balances, but NEVER writes the global aggregates s.sys.silo.stalk or s.sys.silo.roots. findings.title: Replayable L2 migration inflates account roots, stealing earned-Bean snapshot share
findings.description: L2ContractMigrationFacet.redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances is permissionless and verifies only a Merkle proof over (owner, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots) plus an EIP-712 signature over (owner, reciever, deadline). It stores NO spent/redeemed marker and uses NO nonce. setStalk then does `s.accts[reciever].roots += ownerRoots;` (L2ContractMigrationFacet.sol#207) and `s.accts[reciever].stalk += accountStalk;` (#206) with accumulating adds. Because the proof and signature are public on-chain calldata and there is no replay guard, anyone can re-submit the same redeem call repeatedly before `deadline`, each time adding `ownerRoots` to the reciever's roots and `accountStalk` to its stalk. `roots` is the account's snapshot SHARE in the earned-Bean distribution (LibSilo._balanceOfEarnedBeans, LibSilo.sol#689: stalk*accountRoots/totalRoots). Inflated account roots directly inflate the holder's claim on every future season's minted Beans, drawn from the shared earnedBeans pool that belongs to honest stalkholders. This is the snapshot-consumer view of the replay defect; the replay/access-control root cause is owned by the access_control/logic specialists (DT-003).
findings.impact: An attacker (or any griefer) replays a victim's public migration proof N times, multiplying the reciever's roots and stalk by N. The inflated roots steal a proportionally larger share of every subsequent season's earned-Bean mint from honest stalkholders, and the inflated stalk distorts all Stalk-weighted accounting. With ownerRoots attacker-influenced only via the signed leaf, the cap is the deadline window and gas. Unbacked snapshot weight => earned-Bean theft.
findings.proof_of_concept: 1) Victim/owner publishes a valid (proof, signature, ownerRoots) by calling redeem once (reciever = victim). 2) Attacker observes the calldata. 3) Before deadline, attacker re-calls redeemDepositsAndInternalBalances with the identical (owner, reciever, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots, proof, signature). verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances and verifySignature both pass (pure functions of the same inputs). setStalk adds ownerRoots again. 4) Repeat k times. Assert s.accts[reciever].roots before = R, after k replays = (k+1)*R. 5) Next sunrise mints E earned Beans; reciever's _balanceOfEarnedBeans share scales with its inflated roots, draining honest holders' share of E.
findings.recommendation: Record a per-leaf redeemed marker (e.g. mapping(bytes32 => bool) keyed by the Merkle leaf or by (owner)) and require(!redeemed) / set it before setStalk. Alternatively bind a nonce into the signed struct and consume it. This is the same fix surface as the access_control/logic replay finding (DT-003); coordinate to avoid duplicate submission.

findings.title: L2 reseed leaves global silo.stalk/roots = 0 (div-by-zero DoS / desync)
findings.description: On L2 the Beanstalk Diamond is freshly initialized and farmer state is re-issued by the reseed init facets. ReseedSilo.reseedSiloDeposit sets per-account stalk (s.accts[account].stalk = accountStalk) and per-token global balances (s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited/.depositedBdv), but it NEVER writes the protocol-wide accumulators s.sys.silo.stalk or s.sys.silo.roots. ReseedSun.init sets season/temperature/seedGauge and re-runs LibCases.setCasesV2 but does not touch silo.stalk/roots. InitReseed.init sets paused/isFarm/earnedBeans=0/season but not silo.stalk/roots. A full-repo search confirms s.sys.silo.stalk and s.sys.silo.roots are assigned ONLY by incremental production paths (LibSilo.mintActiveStalk/burnActiveStalk, LibGerminate, LibReceiving) and by mocks (MockSiloFacet.setStalkAndRoots) — never by any init/reseed contract. Therefore immediately after the L2 upgrade completes, accounts collectively hold millions of stalk (s.accts[].stalk > 0) while the globals are s.sys.silo.stalk == 0 and s.sys.silo.roots == 0. This breaks the core Silo invariant total stalk == sum(account stalk) and bricks the standard burn/transfer accounting.
findings.impact: Two concrete consumer outcomes, both High: (1) DoS / division-by-zero. LibSilo.burnActiveStalk computes `roots = s.sys.silo.roots.mul(stalk).div(s.sys.silo.stalk)` and transferStalk computes `s.sys.silo.roots.sub(1).mul(stalk).div(s.sys.silo.stalk)`; with silo.stalk == 0 these revert (div by zero) the first time any migrated farmer withdraws, transfers stalk, plants, or converts — a broad post-migration freeze of withdrawals/transfers. (2) Accounting desync / mis-scaled rewards. mintActiveStalk takes its `roots==0` branch (roots = stalk * rootsBase) so the first depositor after migration mints roots against a global stalk that does not include the millions of already-issued account stalk; the global stalk/roots ratio is anchored to a single new deposit, so subsequent root issuance and burnActiveStalk proportions are computed against a total stalk far smaller than the true sum of account stalk. Earned-Bean distribution (LibSilo._balanceOfEarnedBeans uses silo.stalk*accountRoots/silo.roots) and LibGauge.getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv (silo.stalk/totalBdv) are mis-scaled. The migration upgrade thus either freezes core Silo operations or corrupts protocol-wide stalk/root accounting depending on which path executes first.
findings.proof_of_concept: Post-migration state (no attacker needed): assume ReseedSilo issued account A 1_000_000 stalk and there are no other deposits. State: s.accts[A].stalk = 1_000_000, s.accts[A].roots = 0, s.sys.silo.stalk = 0, s.sys.silo.roots = 0. (1) A calls a withdraw -> LibSilo.burnActiveStalk(A, 1_000_000) -> roots = silo.roots(0) * 1_000_000 / silo.stalk(0) -> division by zero -> revert. Withdrawal impossible. (2) Alternatively a fresh depositor B deposits, hits mintActiveStalk roots==0 branch, sets silo.stalk = B.stalk (small) and silo.roots = B.stalk*rootsBase; now total silo.stalk excludes A's 1_000_000 -> every downstream ratio (burn, transfer, earned beans) is computed against the wrong total, so A's stalk is unredeemable/mis-valued. A Foundry PoC would deploy the reseed init, vm.load s.sys.silo.stalk slot to assert == 0 while s.accts[A].stalk != 0, then expect revert on a withdraw call (L2 entry, EOA, no privileged setup beyond the migration itself).
findings.recommendation: In the L2 reseed sequence, after all per-account stalk/roots are issued, set the global accumulators to the exact sums: s.sys.silo.stalk = sum(all account stalk issued) and s.sys.silo.roots = sum(all account roots issued) (or seed roots = stalk * C.getRootsBase() consistently and set both account and global roots accordingly). Add an init-completion invariant check asserting s.sys.silo.stalk == sum(s.accts[].stalk) and that silo.roots > 0 before unpausing. Cross-check against ReseedSun/InitReseed so exactly one init step is responsible for the global totals.

findings.title: Migration merkle leaf omits reciever; destination bound only by signature
findings.recommendation: Include `reciever` in the merkle leaf preimage (keccak256(abi.encode(account, reciever, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots))) so the immutable root commits to both what migrates and where it goes, binding destination at the same authorization layer as the asset data.
findings.description: verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances computes the merkle leaf as keccak256(abi.encode(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots)) (line 127). The destination `reciever` is NOT part of the leaf and therefore not committed to by the immutable MERKLE_ROOT. The only thing binding the credit to a specific L2 destination is the owner's EIP-712 signature over (owner,reciever,deadline) in verifySignature. This splits authorization across two artifacts (a root that fixes WHAT migrates, and a signature that fixes WHERE it goes) without binding them together. Because the signature is plain calldata and AC-001 allows unlimited replay, the receiver binding provides no protection against reuse, and the absence of `reciever` from the proof means the proof can never constrain the destination. If a publisher ever signs more than one (owner,reciever) pair for the same owner-leaf, or the signature is otherwise obtainable, credit destination is governed solely by an unprotected, replayable signature rather than by the committed root. This weakens the authorization model and compounds AC-001.
findings.impact: Authorization of the migration destination is decoupled from the merkle commitment and rests entirely on a single unprotected signature. Combined with AC-001 (no nonce/spent-marker) the destination binding is ineffective against replay. Standalone: incorrect/weak access binding of migrated credit. Immunefi v2.2: incorrect access binding without standalone direct loss = Medium.

Show that verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances accepts the proof for ANY `reciever` argument, since reciever is absent from the leaf. 3. The only gate on reciever is verifySignature; demonstrate that the same proof validates under two different reciever values given two different owner signatures, proving the root does not constrain destination. L2: leaf recomputed in test equals the rooted leaf regardless of reciever. L3: migrated credit destination is governed by signature alone, not by the on-chain commitment.

findings.title: getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv underflows when total stalk-per-BDV falls below STALK_BDV_PRECISION, reverting stepGauge and bricking season advancement
findings.description: LibGauge.getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv computes `s.sys.silo.stalk.div(totalBdv).sub(STALK_BDV_PRECISION)` where STALK_BDV_PRECISION = 1e4. The subtraction uses LibRedundantMath256.sub (checked) and there is NO floor/guard ensuring `stalk/totalBdv >= 1e4`. The quotient `stalk/totalBdv` is the average stalk units per BDV unit; it is normally >= the base 1e4, but it can drop below 1e4 if the system stalk-to-BDV ratio is depressed. A depressed ratio is directly reachable post-migration: DT-002/ACC-002 zeroes `s.sys.silo.balances[token].deposited/depositedBdv` for migrated tokens while per-account stalk persists (and DT-001/ACC-001 overwrites per-account stalk), desyncing the global stalk and global BDV totals that feed getTotalBdv() and s.sys.silo.stalk. It is also approachable by large active-stalk burns (mass withdraw/convert) outpacing BDV reduction. When `stalk/totalBdv < 1e4`, the checked .sub reverts. getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv -> updateAverageStalkPerBdvPerSeason -> updateGrownStalkEarnedPerSeason -> stepGauge() reverts, and stepGauge is invoked during sunrise/gm, so every season advance reverts: a protocol-wide temporary freeze until the ratio is externally restored.

Season advancement DoS (temporary protocol freeze) whenever the global stalk/BDV ratio is pushed below 1e4. Immunefi v2.2: temporary freezing of season progression / core protocol function -> High when chained with the migration desync that makes it reachable; standalone (requires the ratio precondition) it is Medium.

findings.title: Migration EIP-712 domain separator hardcodes L1 chainId and lacks any per-message nonce or destination-L2 binding, enabling cross-deployment/multi-L2 signature reuse
findings.description: The migration permit is signed on L1 and verified on L2. _domainSeparatorV4() builds the domain with C.getLegacyChainId() (a hardcoded constant = 1, Ethereum mainnet) and address(this). The struct hash covers only (owner, reciever, deadline) — there is no nonce and no field identifying the specific destination L2 / L2 Beanstalk deployment. Consequently a single owner signature is valid on any L2 deployment whose migration facet shares the same address(this) and the same hardcoded legacy chainId domain, and it carries no monotonically increasing nonce to bound reuse. This is the cross-chain authorization-scoping weakness underlying CC-001/CC-003: the permit is not scoped to a single chain/deployment nor to a single use. If Beanstalk migrates to (or redeploys on) more than one L2, or the diamond address is deterministic across L2s, the same signature is replayable across each.
findings.impact: Cross-deployment / multi-L2 replay of a single migration signature and absence of a nonce that would otherwise bound CC-001. On a single-L2 deployment the practical impact is subsumed by CC-001; the standalone severity (signature not scoped to destination chain + no nonce) is Medium. The hardcoded legacy chainId also means the domain does not reflect the actual L2, so any future chainId-based replay protection is absent.

Steps:
1. Show _domainSeparatorV4 uses getLegacyChainId() == 1 and address(this); compute the domain on two L2 deployments sharing the diamond address and show they are identical.
2. Show the struct hash has no nonce field; produce one signature and demonstrate verifySignature accepts it on each deployment.
3. Combined with CC-001 (no spent marker), demonstrate the same signature credits multiple deployments / multiple times.

findings.title: LibUsdOracle 1e24/price no zero-check: frozen feed reverts, DoSing sunrise
findings.description: In the encodeType 0x01 branch, getTokenPriceFromExternal returns `uint256(1e24).div(LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(addr, FOUR_HOUR_TIMEOUT, lookback))`. LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice — through both getPrice() and getTwap() — is explicitly documented and coded to RETURN 0 (not revert) when the feed is broken or frozen: it returns 0 on a decimals() revert, a latestRoundData() revert, roundId==0, or a stale/invalid timestamp/answer (LibChainlinkOracle.sol L67/L79/L81/L87 and L109/L121/L123/L151/L161). When that 0 is fed into `1e24.div(0)`, the division reverts (LibRedundantMath / Solidity panic 0x12) instead of degrading gracefully. The whole pricing call therefore reverts during a feed outage, contrary to the 0-sentinel contract the rest of the file relies on. This is DT-007 and violates ARITH-003. (Note: this DoS is independent of the inverted ternary in DT-006/OR-001 — whichever helper is selected, a frozen feed yields 0 and the unguarded division reverts.)
findings.impact: When a Chainlink feed backing a whitelisted token (encodeType 0x01) is frozen, stale beyond FOUR_HOUR_TIMEOUT, or reverting, every consumer of getUsdPrice/getTokenPriceFromExternal for that token reverts instead of receiving the documented 0 sentinel. Consumers include the sunrise oracle step and convert pricing; a reverting price call can block season advancement and conversions for the affected token during the outage. Temporary availability DoS gated by an external feed condition (not attacker-triggered). Medium under Immunefi v2.2 (temporary DoS of a core flow). Strong KB precedent (Solodit ~0.58: Chainlink frozen/phase-change feed DoS, Medium).

Assert: with a healthy feed the call returns a finite price; with the frozen feed the identical call reverts (panic 0x12), and the calling sunrise/convert path reverts with it.
findings.recommendation: Check the price before dividing: `uint256 p = LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(...); if (p == 0) return 0; return uint256(1e24).div(p);` so a feed outage degrades to the documented 0 sentinel instead of reverting.

findings.title: LibFlood.calculateSopPerWell div-by-(i-1)=0 reverts flood path in sunrise
findings.description: calculateSopPerWell distributes the flood (Season of Plenty) reduction across positive-deltaB wells. Its final loop runs `for (uint256 i = positiveDeltaBCount; i > 0; i--)` and, inside the branch `if (shaveToLevel > uint256(wellDeltaBs[i-1].deltaB))`, executes `shaveToLevel += (shaveToLevel - uint256(wellDeltaBs[i-1].deltaB)) / (i - 1);`. On the final iteration `i == 1`, so `(i - 1) == 0` and the expression divides by zero, reverting (panic 0x12) whenever that branch is taken for the last (largest, since wells are sorted descending in getWellsByDeltaB) positive well. calculateSopPerWell is called by LibFlood.handleRain, which runs in the flood/Season-of-Plenty branch reached during sunrise (SeasonFacet.gm -> stepSun/weather -> handleRain). When the configuration is mixed-sign (at least one positive and one non-positive well, totalPositiveDeltaB >= totalNegativeDeltaB) and the accumulated shaveToLevel exceeds the largest positive well's deltaB on the final step, the flood computation reverts — and because handleRain executes within the season-advance flow, the revert propagates and blocks that sunrise. Not present in deep-trace; surfaced directly from source.
findings.impact: In a multi-well configuration with mixed-sign deltaBs during a Season of Plenty, the per-well sop allocation can divide by zero and revert. Because the flood logic runs inside the sunrise (gm) call, that revert blocks season advancement for the affected season until the deltaB distribution changes (e.g. reserves shift across a block). Conditional, configuration-dependent temporary DoS of sunrise during flood. Medium under Immunefi v2.2 (season/sunrise DoS, conditional). Currently bounded by the live whitelist having few soppable wells, hence not High.
findings.proof_of_concept: Requires >=2 soppable whitelisted wells with mixed-sign instantaneous deltaB so positiveDeltaBCount>0, positiveDeltaBCount != length, and totalPositiveDeltaB >= totalNegativeDeltaB, with the largest positive well small enough that the redistributed shaveToLevel exceeds it on the final (i==1) iteration. Under those reserves, calling sunrise during oversaturation routes to handleRain -> calculateSopPerWell -> `/(i-1)` with i==1 -> panic 0x12 revert. Assert: the sunrise tx reverts; with a single positive well (positiveDeltaBCount==length) the early return at the top of calculateSopPerWell is taken and no revert occurs (confirming the branch dependence). NOTE: end-to-end reachability depends on having multiple soppable wells and a specific deltaB shape; consumer is found but the triggering market state must be reproduced on a fork before severity is finalized.
findings.recommendation: Guard the divisor: when `i == 1` the remaining amount has no other well to redistribute to, so set `wellDeltaBs[0].deltaB = 0` (or break) instead of dividing by `i-1`; equivalently restructure the redistribution so the divisor is always > 0.

findings.title: floodPodline mints 0.1% of Bean supply to the Field every Flood season, harvestable in pod (FIFO) order — front-runnable by buying the front of the pod line before an Oversaturation streak
findings.description: LibFlood.floodPodline() makes up to FLOOD_PODLINE_PERCENT_DENOMINATOR^-1 = 0.1% of total Bean supply worth of Pods Harvestable on every flood season (it runs first in the flood branch, before the well SOP). Harvestable Pods are consumed strictly in pod-line (FIFO) index order. Because a Flood is permissionlessly triggerable via sunrise/gm() once Beanstalk has been Oversaturated for a season, and because the marketplace lets Pods near the front of the line be purchased, a well-capitalized actor who anticipates an Oversaturation streak can accumulate the front-most Pods (or sow into the front) cheaply and then permissionlessly drive the flood seasons to ripen 0.1% of supply per season directly into those positions. The reward is bounded (0.1% of supply per season, capped by maxHarvestable) and the front-of-line Pods are a public, priced market, so this is opportunistic value capture / reward-timing rather than theft of others' principal — hence Medium, not High.
findings.impact: An actor timing the controllable Flood schedule can convert held Beans into a near-deterministic stream of Field harvest at the front of the pod line, advantaging informed/MEV-capable participants over passive Pod holders. Bounded to 0.1% of supply per flood season and to the front of the line; no protocol insolvency, but a recurring incentive-timing edge.
findings.proof_of_concept:
1. Beanstalk enters Oversaturation (P>1, pod rate <5%); attacker recognizes the streak will continue.
2. Attacker buys the front-most outstanding Pods on the marketplace (or sows when those plots will be first in line) for X Beans.
3. Each subsequent season the attacker (or anyone) permissionlessly calls sunrise()/gm(); handleRain() flood branch runs floodPodline(), minting min(0.1% of beanSupply, pods-harvestable) Beans into harvestable, consumed FIFO by the attacker's front-line Pods.
4. Attacker harvests; repeated each flood season. Profit = sum of harvested Beans (each up to 0.1% of supply) - purchase cost of the front Pods. Positive when the attacker acquired the front Pods below their post-flood harvest value.

findings.title: Convert stalk-penalty before/after deltaB uses uncapped spot reserves while the convert-capacity ceiling uses the capped pump, letting a flash-loan-skewed well under-report against-peg movement and avoid the stalk penalty
findings.description: The convert stalk-penalty machinery measures how far a convert moves a well's deltaB against the peg using INSTANTANEOUS, UNCAPPED spot reserves, but the capacity ceiling it is compared against is derived from the CAPPED (rate-limited) pump. In LibPipelineConvert.populatePipelineConvertData the 'before' deltaB values (beforeOverallDeltaB, beforeInputTokenDeltaB, beforeOutputTokenDeltaB) are read via LibDeltaB.overallCurrentDeltaB() / getCurrentDeltaB(), and prepareStalkPenaltyCalculation reads the 'after' values via LibDeltaB.scaledOverallCurrentDeltaB() / getCurrentDeltaB(). Both ultimately call LibDeltaB.currentDeltaB(well) -> IWell(well).getReserves() -> calculateDeltaBFromReserves(..., ZERO_LOOKBACK), i.e. the raw spot reserves with no pump cap and no lookback. In contrast, the overall convert capacity (LibPipelineConvert: pipeData.overallConvertCapacity = abs(LibDeltaB.overallCappedDeltaB())) and the per-well capacity (LibConvert.calculatePerWellCapacity: abs(LibDeltaB.cappedReservesDeltaB(well))) are read from ICappedReservesPump.readCappedReserves, which the Multi-Flow Pump rate-limits per block. Because a pipelineConvert executes attacker-supplied advancedFarmCalls (arbitrary Pipeline external calls, incl. flash-loaned swaps) between the 'before' snapshot and the 'after' snapshot, the attacker controls the uncapped spot reserves at both read points. LibConvert.calculateAgainstPeg / calculateConvertedTowardsPeg derive the penalty purely from these before/after spot deltaB pairs. By skewing the uncapped spot deltaB so that the measured 'against-peg' amount (or the towards-peg amount that consumes capacity) is understated relative to the true economic movement, an attacker can reduce or zero the stalkPenaltyBdv that should have applied, and in ConvertFacet.convert specifically force checkForValidConvertAndUpdateConvertCapacity's require(stalkPenaltyBdv == 0) to pass for a convert that, measured on capped reserves, should have been penalized or rejected. The result is the convert keeps more grownStalk (newGrownStalk = initialGrownStalk * (fromBdv - stalkPenaltyBdv) / fromBdv) than the capped-capacity design intends.

location.code_snippet:
pipeData.deltaB.beforeOverallDeltaB = LibDeltaB.overallCurrentDeltaB(); // uncapped spot
...
dbs.afterOverallDeltaB = LibDeltaB.scaledOverallCurrentDeltaB(initialLpSupply); // uncapped spot
// while: pipeData.overallConvertCapacity = LibConvert.abs(LibDeltaB.overallCappedDeltaB()); // capped

findings.impact: Stalk-penalty avoidance / convert-capacity-ceiling bypass: a convert that should incur a stalk penalty (or be rejected in the non-pipeline ConvertFacet.convert path) measures zero/under-stated against-peg movement on flash-loan-skewed spot reserves, so the user retains more grown stalk than the capped capacity intends. This is a relative governance/yield-weight gain and capacity-cap dilution, not a direct unbacked Bean mint (the minted output BDV is bounded by the capped pump per FL via LibWellBdv). Medium: economic/accounting integrity of the convert penalty, conditioned on the attacker being able to move the uncapped spot deltaB enough within the pipeline relative to the capped reading.
findings.proof_of_concept: L1 (entry): EOA calls PipelineConvertFacet.pipelineConvert(inputWell, stems, amounts, outputToken, advancedFarmCalls) with no privileged setup; the advancedFarmCalls include a flash-loaned swap against the input/output well to skew its instantaneous spot reserves. L2 (state flip): assert the value read by LibDeltaB.overallCurrentDeltaB()/getCurrentDeltaB() (IWell.getReserves(), uncapped) differs materially from LibDeltaB.overallCappedDeltaB()/cappedReservesDeltaB() (readCappedReserves, capped) at the same block; show calculateAgainstPeg(before,after) on the skewed spot pair returns a lower against-peg amount than it would on capped reserves, so applyStalkPenalty returns stalkPenaltyBdv smaller than the capped-reserve value. L3 (outcome): assert newGrownStalk = initialGrownStalk*(fromBdv - stalkPenaltyBdv)/fromBdv is larger than under capped accounting (extra grown stalk retained), and for ConvertFacet.convert assert the require(stalkPenaltyBdv == 0) passes for a convert that capped-reserve accounting would penalize. NOTE: the magnitude depends on how far getReserves() can diverge from readCappedReserves() within a single block; if the live well's reserves and the cap rate make that divergence small, the realized penalty-avoidance is small. This must be quantified against the deployed pump cap before escalating severity.
findings.recommendation: Measure the stalk-penalty before/after deltaB from the SAME capped/instantaneous pump source used for the capacity ceiling (readCappedReserves / readInstantaneousReserves), not from raw IWell.getReserves(). Using uncapped spot for the penalty while capping the capacity gives an attacker a manipulable lever on exactly the value the cap is meant to bound.

ite.technique: Skew the well's uncapped spot reserves with flash-loaned swaps inside the pipeline's advancedFarmCalls between the before and after deltaB reads, since the penalty math (calculateAgainstPeg/calculateConvertedTowardsPeg) consumes spot deltaB while the capacity ceiling consumes capped deltaB.
ite.evasion: The capacity ceiling LOOKS like a robust per-block cap (capped pump), masking that the penalty's before/after deltaB it is compared against is read from the uncapped spot pump and is fully attacker-controllable within the same transaction.

findings.title: LibWstethEthOracle returns 0 when Chainlink and Uniswap diverge >1% (no documented fallback)
findings.description: getWstethEthPrice computes a Chainlink-derived price and a Uniswap V3 TWAP price, then only assigns wstethEthPrice inside `if (getPercentDifference(chainlinkPrice, uniswapPrice) < MAX_DIFFERENCE)` (1%). When the two sources differ by >=1%, the if-block is skipped and the function returns the default 0. The NatSpec (L29-35) documents a richer policy ('minimum of (3) and either the average of (1) and (2) ... or (1)'), but the implemented code has NO else branch and NO fall-through to source (1) or (3): it simply returns 0. A returned 0 propagates as an oracle-failure sentinel (getUsdPrice/getWstethUsdPrice return 0; LibWell.getRatiosAndBeanIndex sets success=false; LibWellMinting.twaDeltaB treats the minting oracle as 'off' and returns deltaB=0; LibDeltaB.calculateDeltaBFromReserves reverts 'USD Oracle call failed').

findings.title: Arbitrary-call facets (Farm/Depot/Tractor) lack nonReentrant guard
findings.description: Beanstalk's reentrancy defense is a hybrid model: a diamond-wide ReentrancyGuard (shared storage slot s.sys.reentrantStatus) applied to the genuinely sensitive Silo/Convert functions (SiloFacet deposit/withdraw/transfer, ConvertFacet.convert, PipelineConvertFacet.pipelineConvert, EnrootFacet, ClaimFacet, MarketplaceFacet, UnripeFacet.chop) PLUS the Invariable balance/stalk/supply modifiers (fundsSafu, noNetFlow, noOutFlow, oneOutFlow, noSupplyChange/Increase) on everything else. The four general-purpose ARBITRARY EXTERNAL CALL entrypoints that the attack-surface map flags as the prime reentrancy surface -- FarmFacet.farm/advancedFarm, DepotFacet.pipe/multiPipe/advancedPipe/etherPipe, TractorFacet.tractor, and the executeAdvancedFarmCalls window inside LibPipelineConvert -- carry NO nonReentrant modifier (FarmFacet nonReentrant=0, DepotFacet nonReentrant=0, TractorFacet nonReentrant=0). They depend entirely on (a) the shared guard being already set by an outer guarded caller, and (b) the Invariable post-conditions. The architectural consequence: when a user enters through one of these unguarded entrypoints (e.g. FarmFacet.farm or DepotFacet.advancedPipe), the shared reentrant flag is NOT set, so an external call made through Pipeline can re-enter the diamond and reach OTHER unguarded state-mutating functions (FieldFacet.sow/harvest -- 0 guards, SeasonFacet.sunrise/gm -- 0 guards, FertilizerFacet.mintFertilizer/claimFertilized -- 0 guards) while the outer batch is mid-execution. Reentry into a nonReentrant function (any Silo/Convert op) IS correctly blocked by the shared flag once one is active; the gap is the unguarded<->unguarded reentry surface, where the only backstop is the Invariable balance equality/inequality checks evaluated at each modifier's closing brace. Those checks defend token *custody* (balances cannot net-decrease) but do NOT defend internal accounting consistency (stalk attribution, deltaB snapshots, soil/temperature, season state) read mid-batch. This is the structural seam that the economic/oracle reserve-skew vectors (see cross_agent_refs) ride on; on its own it is a Medium reentrancy-surface exposure pending a traced consumer that converts the mid-batch state read into fund loss.

findings.impact: An external call routed through Pipeline/Farm/Depot can re-enter the diamond and reach unguarded state-mutating functions (sow, harvest, sunrise, mintFertilizer) while an outer arbitrary-call batch is mid-execution and internal accounting (stalk/deltaB/season) is transiently inconsistent. Token custody is protected by the Invariable balance modifiers, so direct theft is not demonstrated by reentrancy alone; the realized impact is the enabling seam for the reserve-skew/oracle economic exploits tracked by the flash_loan/oracle/economic agents. Standalone severity Medium (state-read inconsistency, no traced direct drain).
findings.recommendation: Apply the diamond-wide nonReentrant modifier to all general-purpose arbitrary-external-call entrypoints (FarmFacet.farm/advancedFarm, DepotFacet.pipe/multiPipe/advancedPipe/etherPipe, TractorFacet.tractor). This closes the unguarded<->unguarded reentry surface so that no Beanstalk state-mutating function can be re-entered while a Farm/Depot/Tractor/pipelineConvert batch is in flight, regardless of whether the reentered function individually carries the guard. Do not rely solely on Invariable balance checks for reentrancy safety, since they validate custody, not transient internal-accounting consistency.

findings.title: TractorFacet omits Invariable fundsSafu net that sibling entrypoints enforce
findings.recommendation: Make TractorFacet inherit Invariable and wrap tractor() with fundsSafu (and noSupplyIncrease as FarmFacet/DepotFacet do), so the publisher-delegated batch is subject to the same batch-level solvency net as farm()/pipe(). Alternatively, audit-enumerate every diamond selector reachable from a blueprint and prove each fund-moving one carries its own fundsSafu.
findings.description: Beanstalk applies a consistent guard architecture: every external writing facet inherits `Invariable` and wraps fund-touching logic in solvency/flow modifiers. The two arbitrary/batch execution wrappers FarmFacet (`farm`, `advancedFarm`) and DepotFacet (`pipe`, `multiPipe`, `advancedPipe`, `etherPipe`) both inherit Invariable and carry `fundsSafu` (Depot additionally `noSupplyIncrease`). TractorFacet, which executes an arbitrary `AdvancedFarmCall[]` batch via `LibFarm._advancedFarm` (facet.delegatecall) AS THE PUBLISHER (LibTractor._user() returns blueprint.publisher inside the diamond), does NOT inherit Invariable (`contract TractorFacet` with no base) and its `tractor()` entrypoint carries only `verifyRequisition` + `runBlueprint`. It is the sole fund-executing batch entrypoint with no wrapper-level `fundsSafu`/flow guard. This is an asymmetric, incomplete guard relative to the otherwise-uniform Invariable architecture documented in Invariable.sol ('Every external writing function should use as many non-redundant invariant modifiers as possible. Excepting Diamond functions.').
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth solvency loss on the tractor path. Each inner delegatecall into a guarded facet (deposit/withdraw/convert/claim) re-checks `fundsSafu` at its own boundary, so a single inner call cannot leave the protocol insolvent. The residual exposure is that tractor executes a publisher-authorized batch with no batch-level net check: any unguarded inner sink reachable through a blueprint (a facet selector that moves funds but lacks `fundsSafu` itself), or an interleaving that is solvent at each inner checkpoint yet net-adverse across the batch, would execute with the publisher's delegated context and no final solvency assertion. FarmFacet closes exactly this gap with a wrapper `fundsSafu`; Tractor cannot because it does not inherit Invariable.

  FarmFacet.advancedFarm(...)          -> [fundsSafu, withEth]            (Invariable)
  DepotFacet.pipe / multiPipe /
             advancedPipe / etherPipe  -> [fundsSafu, noSupplyIncrease]  (Invariable)
  TractorFacet.tractor(...)            -> [verifyRequisition, runBlueprint]   <- NO fundsSafu, NOT Invariable

As defense-in-depth, guard each init with onlyOwner / LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner or an initializer one-shot flag so the most state-powerful functions are not the least guarded even if accidentally registered.
findings.description: Every live Beanstalk facet is guarded (Invariable + nonReentrant + role/owner where applicable). By contrast all L2 reseed initializers — ReseedSilo.init, ReseedField.init, ReseedBarn.init, ReseedBean.init, ReseedInternalBalances.init, ReseedSun.init, ReseedWhitelist.init — are declared `external` with NO access modifier (no onlyOwner, no LibDiamond.enforceIsContractOwner, no initializer). They perform privileged bulk global-state writes (per-account stalk/roots/deposits, global silo balances, field pods, fertilizer linked list). This is the maximal guard asymmetry in the codebase: the most state-powerful functions are the least guarded. In the standard EIP-2535 pattern these run once via diamondCut's _init delegatecall and their selectors are not added as facets, so they are not attacker-callable post-upgrade. The risk is contingent: if any init selector is mistakenly registered on the diamond, or diamondCut is itself reachable, an attacker re-runs init to re-write global accounting.

If correctly one-shot via diamondCut _init (expected), not externally reachable and the guard asymmetry is by-design for diamond initializers. findings.title: LibTractor domain separator uses wrong typehash (BLUEPRINT not EIP712Domain)
findings.recommendation: Use the dedicated EIP712_TYPE_HASH (EIP712Domain typehash) constant in _domainSeparatorV4() instead of BLUEPRINT_TYPE_HASH so the domain separator matches the EIP-712 standard and signatures produced by standard tooling verify correctly.
findings.description: LibTractor._domainSeparatorV4() (line 173-184) computes the EIP-712 domain separator as keccak256(abi.encode(BLUEPRINT_TYPE_HASH, TRACTOR_HASHED_NAME, TRACTOR_HASHED_VERSION, C.getChainId(), address(this))). It uses BLUEPRINT_TYPE_HASH (the Blueprint struct typehash, line 28) as the domain typehash, while the correctly-defined EIP712_TYPE_HASH constant (the EIP712Domain typehash, line 24-27) is never referenced. This is a malformed domain separator: it does not match the EIP-712 standard digest that off-chain signers / wallets (eth_signTypedData) and verifying tools produce. Note this does NOT create a signature-replay or auth-bypass vulnerability: the same (non-standard) separator is used consistently on-chain by both the signer-recovery path and the verifier, chainId IS included via C.getChainId(), and TractorFacet uses a per-blueprintHash nonce incremented in runBlueprint with a maxNonce ceiling, so blueprint replay is bounded. The impact is interoperability/standards-correctness: signatures produced by a standards-compliant EIP-712 signer will not verify, and any tooling assuming a standard domain will fail. It does not advance to Medium under ICE because no privilege escalation or unauthorized state change results (consumer impact is signature non-verification, i.e. self-DoS of legitimate signers, already a likely usability issue rather than an attacker capability).
findings.impact: Non-standard EIP-712 domain separator: signatures from standard tooling will not verify against Tractor blueprints. No auth bypass, no replay (chainId present, per-blueprint nonce enforced). Severity Low (standards/interoperability correctness).

A blueprint signed via a standards-compliant eth_signTypedData call will fail the verifyRequisition check (signer != publisher).

findings.title: LibUsdOracle chainlink branch divides 1e24 by an unchecked oracle price (division-by-zero revert on frozen/broken feed)
findings.description: getTokenPriceFromExternal, encodeType 0x01 (default chainlink) path, returns `uint256(1e24).div(LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice(addr, FOUR_HOUR_TIMEOUT, lookback))`. LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice/getPrice/getTwap are explicitly documented and coded to RETURN 0 (not revert) when the feed is broken, frozen, has a non-positive answer, or times out. There is NO zero-check before the division here (unlike the WETH/WSTETH branches at lines 52/57/63 which guard `if (price == 0) return 0`). When the underlying chainlink feed returns 0, `1e24 / 0` reverts via LibRedundantMath256.div, instead of the documented graceful 0-return contract. This DoSes any peg/minting/convert path that prices an encodeType-0x01 token while its feed is down. Note the inverted-lookback ternary in LibChainlinkOracle.getTokenPrice (lookback>0 -> spot, lookback==0 -> getTwap(...,0)) is a separate oracle-class bug (ARITH-001); the arithmetic-specific issue here is the missing zero guard before inversion.

Best-practice violation of the documented 0-sentinel contract; severity Low because it requires an external feed outage and only causes a revert (no value extraction).

Season/convert/peg logic that reaches this token's price reverts. consumer_found=true (LibDeltaB / minting / convert price paths). PoC is a unit test stubbing the aggregator to return 0; flagged for runtime confirmation.

findings.title: ReseedInternalBalances: no farmers/balances length check, OOB revert DoS
findings.description: setInternalBalances iterates `i` over `internalBalances.farmers.length` and reads `internalBalances.balances[i]` without first requiring `farmers.length == balances.length`. findings.title: Chainlink oracle ignores answeredInRound and has no min/max price bounds
findings.description: LibChainlinkOracle validates latestRoundData only via roundId!=0 and checkForInvalidTimestampOrAnswer (timestamp non-zero/not-future, within maxTimeout, answer>0). It never checks `answeredInRound >= roundId`, so a carried-over/stale answer from a prior round that still satisfies the timeout passes as fresh. It also applies no min/max sanity bounds on the returned answer, so during a Chainlink mispricing or a feed pinned at its circuit-breaker min/max the out-of-range value is consumed at face value (the protocol has no minAnswer/maxAnswer rejection). Heartbeat handling is coarse: FOUR_HOUR_TIMEOUT (14400s) is applied to feeds the comments describe as 1-hour heartbeat, accepting answers up to 4h stale.

Lower severity because Chainlink is the trusted source, the 0-on-failure design already handles outright outages, and the timeout bounds gross staleness.

findings.description: Within SiloFacet the deposit-transfer group has asymmetric reentrancy guarding. `transferDeposit` (public, L140) and `transferDeposits` (external, L173) carry `fundsSafu noNetFlow noSupplyChange nonReentrant`. findings.title: stalkReward casts a potentially-negative int96 stem delta to uint96 (huge value) with no enforced endStem >= startStem
findings.description: LibSilo.stalkReward computes `uint128(uint96(endStem.sub(startStem))).mul(bdv).div(PRECISION)`. The NatSpec states 'endStem must be larger than startStem' but the code does NOT enforce it. If a caller passed endStem < startStem, the int96 difference is negative and `uint96(negative)` becomes a ~7.9e28-scale value, then `.mul(bdv)` (LibRedundantMath128, checked) overflows uint128 and reverts for any non-trivial bdv. In practice every caller derives startStem from a stored deposit stem and endStem from the current stemTip / germStem.stemTip, and stemTipForToken only grows over time, so startStem <= endStem holds for valid deposits; removeDepositFromAccount / grownStalkForDeposit additionally require stem <= stemTip. Therefore the path is a checked-revert (DoS) at worst and is not attacker-reachable with the invariant intact. Flagged as a robustness gap: an explicit `require(endStem >= startStem)` would replace a silent giant-cast-then-overflow with a clear error.
findings.impact: No value extraction; a malformed (endStem < startStem) call reverts via checked uint128 multiplication rather than returning a wrong reward. Truncation of the final `reward` to uint128 is also safe: (stemDelta * bdv)/1e6 fits uint128 for any realistic Bean BDV. Info.
findings.proof_of_concept: All observed callers (_removeDepositFromAccount, _removeDepositsFromAccount, _balanceOfGrownStalk via __mow, LibConvert._withdrawTokens) pass startStem = deposit stem (<= stemTip) and endStem = stemTip/germStem.stemTip, so endStem >= startStem. No reachable counterexample. consumer_found true but no exploit_path.

findings.title: Unchecked uint128() downcasts of bdv*stalkIssuedPerBdv and gauge average ('safeCast unnecessary' comments) verified safe under realistic bounds
findings.description: Two NatSpec 'safeCast not needed / unnecessary' downcasts were re-derived independently rather than trusted: (1) LibConvert._depositTokensForConvert line 540 `uint128(bdv.mul(LibTokenSilo.stalkIssuedPerBdv(token)))` and (2) LibGauge.updateAverageStalkPerBdvPerSeason line 320 `uint128(getAverageGrownStalkPerBdv().mul(BDV_PRECISION).div(targetSeasonsToCatchUp))`. For (1), stalkIssuedPerBdv is on the order of 1e10 (1 stalk = 1e10 micro-units); overflowing uint128 (~3.4e38) would require bdv > ~3.4e28 micro-BDV, i.e. ~3.4e22 Beans of value, which is many orders of magnitude above any plausible Bean supply (~1e13 micro-Beans). For (2), the divided average is similarly bounded. Both casts are therefore safe in practice; flagged only to record that the comments were verified, not accepted, and that the bound is implicit (not enforced) so a future parameter change to stalkIssuedPerBdv could erode the margin.

findings.title: Fee-on-transfer / rebasing token incompatibility across Silo and convert accounting is gated by privileged whitelist (latent, not permissionlessly reachable)
findings.description: Several non-Silo token sinks use argument-based accounting and/or raw (non-SafeERC20) transfers that would mis-account for fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens: UnripeFacet.addMigratedUnderlying (incrementUnderlying(amount) on the argument; owner-only), LibPipelineConvert.executePipelineConvert (IERC20(inputToken).transfer(C.PIPELINE, fromAmount) raw, then re-measures via transferTokensFromPipeline so the convert leg is partially balance-checked), LibWellConvert (C.bean().transfer raw), LibFlood/LibFertilizer raw approve. None of these tracks a balanceOf delta for the credited amount. However, every token that can flow through these paths is constrained to the governance-managed whitelist / unripe-underlying / Barn-Raise set, and whitelistToken/whitelistTokenWithEncodeType/whitelistTokenWithExternalImplementation are owner-or-Beanstalk gated. The current set (BEAN, BEAN-LP wells, WETH, wstETH) is entirely standard, non-FOT and non-rebasing, so the FOT/rebasing drain class is not reachable by an unprivileged attacker in this deployment. Recorded as Info to flag the latent assumption rather than an exploitable bug.

findings.title: Fertilizer1155 pays out Beans (payFertilizer) inside _beforeTokenTransfer using pre-transfer balances and before the ERC1155 acceptance check
findings.description: Fertilizer1155.safeTransferFrom calls _beforeTokenTransfer -> Fertilizer._update(from)/_update(to) -> IBS(owner()).payFertilizer(account, amount), an external Bean-paying call into Beanstalk, BEFORE _transfer updates the ERC1155 balances and before __doSafeTransferAcceptanceCheck. __update reads _balances[id][account].amount, which for both from and to reflects PRE-transfer balances; that is the intended settle-before-move behavior for the sender but means recipient (to) is settled on its old (often zero) balance, and the Bean payout external call occurs while the 1155 transfer is mid-flight. This is an ERC1155-callback ordering / CEI concern more than an ERC20 non-standard-token issue, and overlaps the reentrancy specialist's lane (Fertilizer is owner-gated to Beanstalk, which has nonReentrant on its facets). No fund-loss path was traced end-to-end from the token-integration angle; flagged for the reentrancy/logic agents to confirm whether a malicious to-contract callback during __doSafeTransferAcceptanceCheck can reenter while fertilizer payout state is mid-update.
